canonical.name: Nonnegatively graded rings and modules, including homogeneous pieces and degree shifts, are fixed before any Hilbert-function argument begins.
The associated graded construction packages the ideal-adic successive quotients into a graded ring and module.
The filtration induced on a submodule from the ambient ideal-adic filtration is equivalent to the submodule's intrinsic ideal-adic filtration.
Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity is defined from the factorial-scaled leading coefficient of the eventual Hilbert-Samuel polynomial.
Passing modulo a parameter preserves the top Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity up to the finite-length annihilator correction.
Parameter-ideal multiplicity is positive by descending to the finite-length case along a parameter chain.

canonical.name: Every faithfully flat ring map is injective because faithful flatness detects the zero ideal as proper only when its preimage is already zero.
Finite generation descends along faithfully flat maps by lifting generators from fibres and applying Nakayama.
